title: Refute Remark C.2.3.2 and Proposition C.2.3.13(2) as printed (AppC Sec2a_part2 Printed)
body:
Sweep of `RiemannMasullo/AppC_LCTVS/Sec2a_part2_F225_F227_Printed.lean`: proves two refutations (ERRATA F225, F226). Only proofs and `private theorem` helpers are added, all in this file, plus `import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.lpSpace`.

Closes #5745
Closes #5746

**`Printed.tensorDualOperator_represents_finiteRank_false`** (Remark C.2.3.2, p. 677). Any normed space E that is not complete gives a counterexample. Take a point h of the completion outside E. Then φ ↦ φ̃(h), into `ULift ℂ`, is rank one and μ-continuous, because the singleton {h} is compact. A tensor in E ⊗ ℂ evaluates functionals at some x ∈ E, and a functional on the completion that separates h from x gives the contradiction. The concrete E is the span of the coordinate vectors in ℓ²(ℕ), which is not closed because (2⁻ⁿ) is a limit of its partial sums.

**`Printed.completedInductiveTensor_directLimits_isEmbedding_false`** (Proposition C.2.3.13(2), p. 683). This uses a variant of the docstring's example: tail subspaces with projections instead of quotients.
- First system: Xₙ = Pₙ(D), where D is the span of the coordinate vectors in ℓ² and Pₙ zeroes the first n coordinates. The transitions are the projections. Its limit is zero, because every finitely supported vector is eventually killed.
- Second system: the single stage ℂ, over `PUnit`. Its limit is Hausdorff because the lift to ℂ is continuous and injective.
- Contradiction: the target is zero, so T sends `of 0 w` to 0. Here w is the image in the completed stage 0 of the completion point of (2⁻ⁿ). By injectivity and `of.zero_exact`, some transition would kill w. But the m-th coordinate functional, extended to the completion, takes the value 2⁻ᵐ ≠ 0 on that transition.

`#print axioms` for both theorems: `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.
